one_line: Guru Nanak, founding teacher of the Sikh tradition, travelling and singing hymns with his companion and rabab-player Bhai Mardana in early 16th-century Punjab.

appearance.age_look: Guru Nanak appears as a calm, sturdy man in his early fifties; Bhai Mardana appears as a lean man in his forties, both with modest traveller’s builds.
appearance.face: Guru Nanak has a broad, gentle face with a warm wheatish-brown complexion, high cheekbones, straight nose, soft but penetrating eyes, and a serene, faintly smiling default expression; Bhai Mardana has a narrower face, slightly darker brown complexion, a straight nose, alert eyes, and an expression of attentive devotion as he listens and plays.
appearance.hair: Guru Nanak’s hair is fully wrapped in a soft, rounded mustard-gold turban tied simple and neat with no ornament, suggesting long hair covered beneath; Bhai Mardana wears a plain white cotton turban tied lower on the forehead with a small, loose tail at the back, both men’s facial hair full and well kept.
appearance.costume: Guru Nanak wears a long, calf-length, straight-cut kurta of soft undyed off-white cotton under a knee-length, sleeveless, mustard-gold chola-style outer robe with simple front opening and narrow side slits, belted loosely with a plain brown cloth sash; over this he drapes a light, unpatterned, warm grey wool shawl around shoulders and chest, modestly covering his torso, with loose off-white cotton salwar trousers gathered at the ankles and simple brown leather sandals; Bhai Mardana wears a knee-length, pale blue-grey cotton kurta over slightly darker blue-grey loose salwar, a thin brown leather waist belt, a light beige shawl thrown over one shoulder for modest warmth, and plain dark brown leather sandals, both men’s clothing simple, unembroidered and appropriate for humble travellers in early 16th-century Punjab.
appearance.signature: Guru Nanak carries a simple, well-used walking staff of dark brown wood with a smooth rounded top, while Bhai Mardana cradles a wooden rabab with a gourd-like resonant body, light-brown polished wood frame, and a dark stringed neck held ready in his hands.

ref_desc: Guru Nanak is a wheatish-brown, broad-faced, serene man in his early fifties with a mustard-gold turban, off-white kurta, mustard-gold sleeveless robe, warm grey shawl, off-white salwar, brown sandals and a dark wooden staff, standing beside lean Bhai Mardana in a white turban, pale blue-grey kurta and salwar with beige shawl and rabab, all in simple early 16th-century Punjabi traveller dress in mustard gold, off-white, warm grey, pale blue-grey and dark brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Guru Nanak and Bhai Mardana as a travelling pair in early 16th-century Punjab: Guru Nanak is a sturdy man in his early fifties with a broad, gentle wheatish-brown face, high cheekbones and soft but penetrating eyes, his default expression calm and faintly smiling; his beard is full and neatly kept, and his hair is entirely covered by a soft, rounded mustard-gold turban tied simply without ornament. He wears a calf-length, straight-cut off-white cotton kurta under a knee-length, sleeveless mustard-gold chola-like outer robe with a simple front opening and narrow side slits, belted loosely at the waist with a plain brown cloth sash; over his shoulders and chest is a modest, light wool warm-grey shawl that drapes his torso, and below are loose off-white salwar trousers gathered at the ankles and simple brown leather sandals. His signature prop is a dark brown wooden walking staff with a smooth rounded top, held lightly in one hand. Beside him, Bhai Mardana is a lean man in his forties with a slightly darker brown complexion, narrower face, straight nose and attentive eyes, expression focused and devoted; he has a full, neat beard and wears a plain white cotton turban tied lower on the forehead. His costume is a knee-length pale blue-grey cotton kurta over slightly darker blue-grey loose salwar, cinched with a thin brown leather waist belt, a light beige shawl draped over one shoulder, and dark brown leather sandals. He cradles a wooden rabab with a gourd-like resonant body, light-brown polished wood frame and dark neck with visible strings, held as if ready to play. Keep everything modest and era-accurate, with no armour or ornament, using a restrained palette of mustard gold, off-white, warm grey, pale blue-grey and dark brown, and show them front and slight-angle views so their turban shapes, robes, shawls, staff and rabab can be consistently redrawn.
